changed.what: Split per the audit note, whose evidence holds. The work in the four sibling repositories (choosing V, landing it in asupersync, frankensim, frankentorch and fastmcp_rust, the mirrored beads, before.tree-d.txt) moves to the new NFp4-01 (deps N33c-07 and STD-E2E, level 2). This bead now depends on NFp4-01 and keeps the root patch, the cargo-metadata check of activated exact requirements, the fixture, the switch-over and the controls. Before the split, sibling work that needs nothing from this workspace waited behind level 13. The fixture now says where before.tree-d.txt comes from, and how observed_at is set when a consumer's first pin already holds the landed change. Without that rule the fixture would pass at the pin and fail BD-037's check.

Now states BD-037's pin_state = unpinned rule, with a matching acceptance clause: the fixture is written at the head of the day, re-run at the pin N33c-24 admits, and the field is then cleared. Without it, nobody owned clearing the row's unpinned state. The e2e call `frob telemetry export-html --json` lacked the run, --world and --out that the VERBS-telemetry row requires, so it would have been refused; it now has all three.

'The Mac run of INT-FLN-01 adds its record beside the Linux one' read as a second gate recording, but BD-380 is the gate's one recorder (convention 9). It now says: an admission record through N33a-07's writer (host.class m5-ultra, with the fingerprint), the receipt hash logged, and no second record_gate call. The acceptance line matches.

Phase post ran `frob sim run --fixture <incline|stack>`, which could not work: neither name is a registered fixture (802); a ten-high stack is over the referee cap (721); the forced retry was placed in the conformance build (802); and it was compared with the undisturbed run, which KA-341 says differs. It now uses BD-080's traction/referee_stand and referee_drop in the chaos build, with --chaos-plan (fail_attempts_below = 1), compared with the clean twin run under --numerical-plan-floor 1. New deps: BD-080, BD-083 (the plan inputs), BD-085 (the referee contact battery it re-runs) and BD-093 (the sill's referee rows need migration). None closes a cycle. The bead's level goes from 54 to 65.

The fixture traction/sphere_on_heightfield was placed under assets/fixtures/traction/. N24b-03 resolves a <space>/<name> reference to crates/frob-conformance/fixtures/<space>/<name>/, so the run as written would not find the fixture (802). Path corrected.

Its switch-over re-runs and its acceptance require the referee's contact battery (BD-085), which the bead did not reach, so the implementer could not run what the acceptance demands. Added BD-085 to deps (no cycle) and updated the scope and the 'may start' sentence.

Phase post registered a new fixture, traction/plate_on_22_points, for the same scene as BD-080's registered traction/referee_capacity_22; it now uses BD-080's fixture. BD-080's test referee_capacity_22_refuses asserts 721 with required = 21, so a capacity-raising form would break it at the new pin with no owner. The bead now re-points that test at capacity + 1 in the pin-move change.

Phase post asserted the registry row reads `adopted`. But N26bp1-01 runs this phase (step 7) before it sets `adopted`, so the phase would always fail. Phase post now asserts `landed`, with the sibling commit and a receipt newer than the pin move.

After the switch-over the bead recorded GATE-GAIT-01 and -02 itself with record_gate. Each gate has one recorder (N22a-38, N22a-39), and those rows were not recorded against a fallback named in advance, so N38b-19 admits no lift. The referee-route re-run is now a check: the receipt hash is logged, there is no record_gate call, and the scope and acceptance match.

The bead said a 'compose' decision closes it as not needed, with the row saying so. But N15b-28, the decision's owner, keeps it open as a P3 convenience item, and BD-037 admits `not-needed` only on FD-FSS-01's row, so the loader would reject that row. Scope, fallback and considerations now follow N15b-28. The acceptance now calls the GATE-SINEW-07 re-run a check, because N15b-30 is its one recorder.

'Both shares are recorded' for the GATE-HAB-09 re-run gave no place and could be read as a second recording; N19b-16 is the gate's one recorder. The shares are now logged with the receipt hash, and no record_gate call is made.

VERBS-ground's ground.identify row now carries --windows <def | raw>, 'Extended by: FD-FSIM-23', and the 724 answer at a pin without the streaming entry. The bead still narrated this as a request of the row (convention 13). It now states the row's form.

The script wrote the peer record to target/e2e-logs/.../peer-<triple>.json and passed it with --peer, but the fixture reads tests/upstream/FD-FSIM-24/peer/<triple>.json. The fixture's cross-machine comparison would therefore never run. --peer now installs the file at the fixture's path.

Phase post called ground.ingest without --emit-variant. Without it no as-built variant is built, so the acceptance line on the variant's route and the new ModelId (GATE-GROUND-08) could not be checked. The option is added; N30a-47, its owner, is reached through BD-395.

The bead said the verb-level wrench check belongs to N26a-02's script and was 'requested of N26a-02' (a convention 13 narration). N26a-02 actually carries the hand case as its unit test push_frame_kept and says no script holds a verb-level form. The bead now states that form.

BD-037 now admits `not-needed` on this conditional row. Dropped the interim form ('the value requested of BD-037's schema ... until the schema admits it the row stays open') in step 0 and the '(or open ... while BD-037's schema lacks that value)' acceptance clause, which kept a second, now-wrong closing state and narrated a request (convention 13). Both now state BD-037's rule. The pin_state unpinned rule and the pending exemption were already stated (lines 92-98).

`frob algebra irreps <family> --json` gave no channel space. The algebra.irreps row takes --in/--out or --rep beside the group source, and every form of the call elsewhere passes one. It is now N13-20's gate-loop form: --family <F> --in natural --out natural.

new_beads.why: The sibling half of FD-ASUP-01 (the audit split): choosing V and landing it in asupersync, frankensim, frankentorch and fastmcp_rust, with the mirrored beads and the before.tree-d.txt evidence. It starts from N33c-07's survey (fail-closed: every sibling counted as consumed) instead of the stack-lock pin. It has its own e2e script, scripts/e2e/upstream_fd_asup_01_siblings.sh, and a closing record that FD-ASUP-01 copies.

requests.what: Its M0 child list has no line for the new NFp4-01: 'NFp4-01: upstream asupersync, frankensim, frankentorch, fastmcp_rust: one published asupersync version V chosen and landed in the four repositories (FD-ASUP-01's sibling half)'.

Sections 2 and 3 say FD-ASUP-01 chooses V and changes the four siblings. That work is now its sibling half NFp4-01, a dependency of FD-ASUP-01: FD-ASUP-01 copies NFp4-01's closing record (V, the evidence, the landed commits, the mirror ids) and hands it to the INT-ASUP-01 admission record. constellation_asupersync_matches_cargo_lock is added in FrankenSim by NFp4-01.

FD-FSIM-13's switch-over re-points your test referee_capacity_22_refuses (721 with required = 21) at capacity + 1 spheres, with required equal to the capacity the airlock reads, once a capacity-raising form lands upstream. The test could say now that `required` is the read capacity, not the literal 21.

An FD-ASUP-01-style split (a sibling half plus a here half) would let that work start early, and the NFp2/NFp3 splits already move the ledger side.
